items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sweets [Edison] used to give it to him all the time. We called him Truce... He loved to ride the train... He said, 'I’m going to get on Iron Michael.'

ctx.x: Big George Matthews was a trombone player. He had been a member of the Count Basie band. His claim to fame was a record called Lazy Lady Blues. [Terry vocalizes the trombone melody.] He had a very, very unique style. He was a huge person. He must have been 7 1/2- or 8-feet tall, and he was big, aside from being tall. He played [with] a very strange type of embouchure. He played almost out of the corner of his mouth. I don’t know how. It must have been this side, because [Terry vocalizes a few notes] you could…

Big George Matthews. He never liked to fly. He had a West Indian accent, and Sweets [Edison] used to give it to him all the time. We called him Truce, T-r-u-c-e, because that was his pet word. He say, “Hey.” “What’s happening there?” “Truce, truce.” He loved to ride the train, because he hated airplanes. He said, “I’m going to get on Iron Michael.” He called the train Iron Michael. “I’m going to get on Iron Michael. I’m going to go home tomorrow.”
